mechanism_narrative: The accelerating week-over-week decline in WORKPLACES (-17.9 to -50.1) signals reduced commuting activity that removes incidental retail visits tied to work trips, driving RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks as fewer people pass by shops during commutes.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES continuing to decline throughout the period, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week transit decline exceeding 6 points reflects tightening of mobility restrictions or public transit curtailment, which mechanically reduces access to retail districts and compresses RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT weekly decline exceeds 6 points (e.g., -6.7 points between t-1w and t-0w)
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell from -30.6 to -37.3 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC stabilizes or rises over the next 2 weeks despite TRANSIT continuing to drop more than 6 points weekly, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increase in RESIDENTIAL (home-dwelling) and decline in WORKPLACES indicate a compounding stay-at-home behavioral shift; when both move in tandem it signals broader lockdown-style compliance that suppresses discretionary retail visits more than either series would alone.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises while WORKPLACES falls in the same week, both exceeding the prior week's pace of change
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose from 2.1 to 5.0 while WORKPLACES fell from -30.6 to -50.1 over the same period
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days even though RESIDENTIAL keeps rising and WORKPLACES keeps falling jointly, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: During a tightening-restrictions regime, a sharp week-on-week surge in PARKS above 15 points reflects substitution of outdoor leisure for indoor retail activity rather than genuine mobility recovery, implying RETAIL_REC continues to contract over the next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 15 points week-on-week (e.g., +18.2 from t-1w to t-0w)
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose from 46.9 to 65.1 between t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises in the week immediately following a PARKS surge exceeding 15 points, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM turning negative after weeks of positive readings signals that restrictions have expanded to cover even essential retail categories, indicating a broader policy clampdown that will further depress RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM crosses from positive to negative week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM fell from 5.4 to -11.6 over four weeks, turning negative at t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC recovers over the next two weeks despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining negative, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: The rise in PARKS mobility reflects seasonal warming rather than policy loosening, so it carries no predictive information for RETAIL_REC; retail recovery depends instead on independent reopening dynamics, meaning PARKS gains do not translate into higher retail footfall over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rose every week while RETAIL_REC fell every week over the snapshot period
failure_condition: If PARKS and RETAIL_REC move together (both rising) over the next four weeks, the decoupling hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A single-week drop in RETAIL_REC exceeding 10 points (here -11.5, from -19.4 to -30.9) indicates an abrupt policy or behavioral shock that typically persists for at least one more week before any stabilization, implying continued decline in RETAIL_REC over the following week.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC fell from -19.4 to -30.9 between t-1w and t-0w, an 11.5 point drop
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rebounds (increases) in the week immediately following an 11.5-point single-week decline, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When RETAIL_REC and WORKPLACES both post their largest weekly declines simultaneously, it suggests the shock has reached a floor consistent with hard-lockdown saturation, after which a modest rebound in RETAIL_REC often follows within a week as essential activity re-stabilizes.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC and WORKPLACES both decline more than 10 points in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC fell 11.5 points and WORKPLACES fell 19.5 points in the same week (t-1w to t-0w)
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC continues falling for another week after the joint sharp decline in RETAIL_REC and WORKPLACES, rather than rebounding, the hypothesis is rejected.
